senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; רָבָה) [large amount,] myriad, ten thousand.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Peah 3:8">Peah III, 8</cite> <he>אחד בר׳ שבהן</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>מר׳</he>) one ten thousandth portion of my property; <cite ref="Tosefta Peah 1:13">Tosef. ib. I, 13</cite>, a. e.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 1:1:22">Y. Maas. Sh. I, 52ᵈ</cite> top <he>מאה ר׳</he> one hundred myriads (of Denars).
<cite ref="Sukkah 51b:6">Succ. 51ᵇ</cite> <he>ששים ר׳ על ששים ר׳ וכ׳</he> twice sixty myriads, double the number &c., v. <cite ref="K01028"><he>כֵּפֶל</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Sukkah 51b:6">Ib.</cite> <he>אינה … וחמשה ר׳ דינרי זהב</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>ואחד</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) worth no less than twenty-five myriads of gold Denars; <cite ref="Tosefta Sukkah 4:6">Tosef. ib. IV, 6</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 913:4">Yalk. Deut. 913</cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Shekalim 8:5">Shek. VIII, 5</cite> <he>משמונים ושתי ר׳ נעשית</he> it (the curtain) was made of material worth eighty-two myriads; (oth. opin.: of eighty-two myriads of threads; Var. <he>ריבות</he> made by eighty-two girls); <cite ref="Chullin 90b:15">Ḥull. 90ᵇ</cite> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 6); a. fr.—Pl. <he>רבּוֹאוֹת</he>, <cite ref="T00053"><he>רִי׳</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 4:3">Arakh. IV, 3</cite> (<cite ref="Arakhin 17b:17">17ᵇ</cite>) <he>אפי׳ מת … ריבוא או ובאה לו בר׳ וכ׳</he> even if his father died (was dying at the time of his vow), and left him a myriad, or he has a ship at sea (at the time of his vow), and it comes in with myriads, the sanctuary has no claim on it.—
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 942:24">Yalk. Deut. 942</cite> <he>שתי רִיבּוֹת</he> two myriads (Zuzin); Sifré <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 306:1">ib. 306</cite> <he>שתי ריבוא</he>.
